risk_rationale.R2: Lowest numerical risk: consolidate persistence and integrity mechanics while freezing every released format, byte representation, error, and restart result.
risk_rationale.R4: Medium numerical risk: share stepping and progress primitives only after checkpoint compatibility is stable; preserve arithmetic and transform order exactly.
risk_rationale.R5: High hot-path risk: unify four pressure-PCG control flows while preserving production, transpose, implicit-backward, and oracle arithmetic, diagnostics, gradients, timing, and memory.
risk_rationale.R1: Highest breadth risk: replace repeated model-geometry construction dispatch across eight application-stack layers only after all lower-level state and solver contracts are stable.

R2.title: Checkpoint and integrity helper consolidation
R2.objective: Make production and functional checkpoint paths share internal integrity, manifest, payload, canonical-metadata, and atomic-publication primitives without changing a released carrier or reader.
R2.planned_internal_owner: pssolver.io; a new private helper module is allowed only if it remains outside the public API and preserves all call-site behavior
frozen_or_reader_only_surfaces: all v0.2.x functional and production format readers and explicit migrations
the released v0.3.0 Plane format 3, legacy Channel format 3, finite-Q format 2, and experimental-shadow format 2 readers
legacy experimental checkpoint carriers that are still required for read compatibility
exact_requirements: current-format output directory trees and metadata bytes are identical
exception class, message, operation, and metadata are identical
fast and NFS-compatible atomic publication semantics are unchanged
imported state and one-step or twenty-step restart results are bitwise identical
source checkpoint directories remain read-only
batch_specific_evidence: all committed functional_checkpoint_releases_v1, legacy_channel_checkpoints_v1, v0_2_0_checkpoints_v1, historical_cpu_coverage_v1, and s09_legacy_compatibility_v1 fixtures
v0.3.0-tag-generated current-format fixtures for Plane, Periodic, legacy Channel, complete-stress Channel, finite-Q, and experimental shadow
byte-tree comparison of current writers against both v0.3.0 and the batch parent
tamper, missing-file, wrong-format, unsupported-version, existing-target, and fail-closed fault matrices
N-1 publication matrix as a CPU contract; a real-NFS rerun is required only if the publication implementation is touched
s19_gpu_scope: CUDA checkpoint and restart for every production and functional family
CPU-to-CUDA and CUDA-to-CPU compatibility cases already in the qualification contract
device-independent identity and installed-wheel import provenance
R2.control_boundary: No Functional API name, semantic, version, beris_edwards blob, or q_tensor blob change is planned. Control main needs only its normal installed-wheel CPU compatibility gate.

R4.planned_internal_owner: pssolver.integrators; shared primitives must be callbacks over the existing arithmetic rather than a reordered vectorized implementation
exact_requirements: same Python and tensor operation order for every field
same in-place versus out-of-place behavior and alias ownership
same real-first transform execution order and transform counts
same refresh_due decision, completed_steps, step_count, refresh_count, and generation values
same callback timing and exception boundary
same restart state at every refresh boundary

refresh intervals None, 1, 2, and a non-divisor of the run length

exact callback order, transform count, progress metadata, and runtime/configuration identity comparisons

CUDA transform execution order and counters
CUDA restart and long-running finite-state checks
R4.control_boundary: No Functional API or constitutive blob change is planned. If sharing requires a public Functional API semantic change, R4 stops and the D-0017 Control-first gate runs before any Provider push.

same warm-start cache semantics and D-0013-adjudicated production behavior

zero RHS, exact-zero residual, nonfinite input/intermediate, operator breakdown, preconditioned-residual breakdown, roundoff-floor crossing, rollback, and iteration-limit cases

R1.objective: Replace repeated per-pair application construction stacks with one immutable registry while preserving every registered key, dispatch result, capability report, error, compiler adapter, runtime, workflow, and identity.

switch one internal dispatch entry point only after shadow parity passes
retain a direct legacy negative control during the batch review

same pre-allocation validation and failure classes/messages
same lowering and binding records and their canonical identities
same selected compiler, application adapter, runtime, workflow, and public capability output
same state traces, runtime_identity, configuration_identity, and installed-wheel behavior
batch_specific_evidence: exhaustive registered-key and near-miss key matrix
shadow versus legacy lowering, binding, compiler, application, runtime, workflow, and identity comparison
all public Simulation construction and dry-run cases

R1.control_boundary: R1 must not alter Functional API 1.1 or either constitutive blob. If the registry cannot be implemented behind those frozen surfaces, Provider work stops and Control main is migrated and CPU-qualified first under D-0017.

control_first_contract.pre_push_rule: Any change to Functional API names, semantics, or version, or to either pinned blob, requires an isolated Control-main migration and CPU qualification before the Provider change may be pushed or released.

s19_handoff.failure_budget: at most one separately authorized diagnostic job after the qualification job
